# Cost Curve & Pricing Strategy

> All figures are **illustrative estimates** built from the stated assumptions. They are not company data.

## Cost Model

**What is being costed:** the DAII gateway is a usage-based capability. It runs on every inference request generated by every user in an enterprise customer and performs:

- per-user rate limiting
- model routing, across both operator-hosted and externally hosted models
- inference-location routing: disaggregated prefill/decode serving, KV-cache-aware routing, latency-based and **network-aware** routing
- batching
- prompt caching and semantic caching

**How AI is used:** the intelligence runs on **Small Language Models (SLMs), not LLMs**:
- an **embedding SLM** for semantic caching
- a **classifier SLM** for intent- and complexity-based routing
- a **classifier SLM** for basic PII/PHI/PCI detection

All other capabilities are deterministic software. An **offline LLM judge** reviews a redacted sample of requests *after* they are processed, to improve future routing. It is never in the request path.

**What DAII does not pay for:** the customer pays its LLM providers directly. DAII **does not resell tokens**, so token pass-through costs are **Not Applicable**. Our cost of goods sold (COGS) covers only the gateway itself.

**Reference customer (Starter tier):**
- 5,000 AI users
- 10M governed requests per month (about 2,000 per user)
- about 2K tokens per request
- the customer's own LLM spend: about **$100K per month** (20B tokens at a blended ~$5 per million tokens)

| Cost Category | Per-User/Month | Notes |
|--------------|----------------|-------|
| Inference (primary model) | **$0.002** | The three runtime SLMs, self-hosted at operator points of presence. About $1 per million requests, so $10/month for 10M requests. |
| Inference (cascading/triage) | **$0.07** | *Adapted for SLM: this covers offline evaluation, not an LLM cascade.* Offline LLM judge on a 1% redacted sample ($100/month), plus a fixed sample of 25K requests per month replayed through the customer's default model to measure quality and savings against the baseline ($250/month). |
| Infrastructure | **$0.30** | High-availability gateway nodes at 2+ points of presence, GPU slice, monitoring: $1,500/month. |
| Data/storage | **$0.03** | Metadata-only logs with audit retention for regulated customers. No prompt content is stored. $150/month. |
| Human-in-the-loop | **$0.20** | Shared analyst queue for medium-confidence guardrail events, plus ML-ops review before router releases: $1,000/month. |
| **Total AI COGS** | **≈ $0.60** | **≈ $3,010/month**, against $9,000 Starter revenue ($1.80 per user), so **~67% gross margin**. |

**Gross margin by tier (illustrative):**

| Tier | Requests/month | Revenue/month | COGS/month | Gross margin |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Starter | 10M | $9,000 | $3,010 | **67%** |
| Growth | 50M | $35,000 | $6,150 | **82%** |
| Enterprise | 250M | $120,000 | $16,350 | **86%** |
| Blended (customer mix 40/40/20) | — | $41,600 avg | $6,930 avg | **~83%** |

Fixed per-customer costs (infrastructure, human review, baseline replay) dominate at small scale. Variable cost is only about **$16 per million requests**, so margin expands with volume.

## Cascading Strategy

> **Adapted for SLM.** The template assumes cheap-model → frontier-model routing *inside our own product*. DAII's own runtime has no frontier model, so that version is **Not Applicable**: DAII is an AI infrastructure product that uses SLMs, not an LLM.
> However, cascading is the **core service DAII performs on the customer's LLM traffic**. It is documented here in that form.

**Triage model:** the DAII router SLM (complexity and intent classifier). It runs after two cheaper, deterministic steps:

1. **Rules:** rate limits, policy checks, data-residency tags and exact-match cache.
2. **Semantic cache:** the embedding SLM checks whether an equivalent request was already answered. The cache is scoped per user and permission context (see M4).
3. **Router SLM:** picks the model tier and the inference location.

**Frontier model:** the customer's designated **default model**, typically a frontier model in a hyperscaler or a frontier lab's API. DAII escalates to it only when the router predicts that a cheaper tier would fall short on quality.

**Routing rule:**
- Send the request to the **cheapest tier** whose predicted quality meets the threshold for that request's preference setting (minimize cost / maximize accuracy / minimize latency).
- Among locations that satisfy the data-residency policy, choose the one with the best predicted end-to-end latency, using operator network congestion data where available.
- If router confidence is below 70%, **fail up** to the default model.
- A semantic re-prompt (the user asks again in different words) escalates one tier.

**Expected cascade ratio (customer traffic):**
- ~15–25% served from cache (no model call)
- ~50–60% served by small or mid-size models
- ~20–30% sent to the frontier model

For reference, RouteLLM reached 95% of GPT-4's quality while sending only 26% of calls to GPT-4. It reported cost reductions of 35–85% depending on the benchmark. DAII plans for **35–60% savings**.

## Pricing Model

**Current pricing:** none. DAII is a new product. The operator currently sells enterprise connectivity (wireline, wireless, SD-WAN), and AI traffic rides on it as ordinary traffic.

**Proposed AI pricing:** a tiered platform fee by governed requests per month.

| Tier | Included requests/month | Platform fee | Overage |
|---|---|---|---|
| Starter | up to 10M | $9,000 | $0.90 per 1K requests |
| Growth | up to 50M | $35,000 | $0.70 per 1K requests |
| Enterprise | up to 250M | $120,000 | $0.45 per 1K requests |

- **Base tier includes:** routing, caching, rate limiting, basic PII/PHI/PCI redaction. Regulated buyers can't route without redaction, so it's in the base.
- **Add-ons, priced separately:** Advanced Security Guardrails (prompt-injection and jailbreak detection, content moderation, red-team reports) and Observability (cost by user and group, compliance reporting). The margin analysis above **excludes** add-on revenue, so add-ons are upside.
- **Network bundle:** 10–15% discount when attached to an existing enterprise network contract. At a 15% discount, blended gross margin falls from about 83% to about 80%.

**Savings are reported, not billed.** DAII shows estimated savings against the customer's default model in the Observability dashboard (method in M4). This proves value at renewal.

**Value check:** the Starter reference customer spends about $100K/month on LLMs. At 35–60% savings that is $35–60K/month saved, against a $9K fee.

**Model:** **hybrid**. A committed platform fee with usage bands and overage, plus optional add-ons.

**Break-even:**
- Fixed operating cost: about $6M per year (about 20 FTEs, baseline point-of-presence capacity, go-to-market).
- Average contribution per customer: about $34.7K/month (~$416K/year).
- Run-rate break-even at **about 15 customers**. With recovery of about $5M initial build cost over 3 years, **about 19 customers** at the assumed mix.

## Stress Tests

| Scenario | Impact on Margin | Response |
|----------|-----------------|----------|
| Inference costs 3x (our GPU costs) | Starter 67% → ~59%; blended 83% → **~78%**. Offline evaluation is the biggest GPU line. | Cut judge sampling from 1% to 0.5%. Move the classifier SLMs to CPU or quantized inference. Pricing unchanged. |
| Heaviest segment doubles | Enterprise customers at 500M requests: about +$112K/month overage revenue against about +$8K/month COGS. **Margin improves.** | The risk is GPU capacity at points of presence, not margin. Secure committed capacity and route overflow to regional or neocloud locations. |
| Model provider raises prices 50% | **No impact on DAII COGS** (no token resale). Platform fee unchanged. | Customer savings *increase*. Publish re-optimized routing policies and highlight the avoided cost at renewal. |
| **Added: token prices fall 10x** | DAII margin unchanged, but **customer value falls**. The Starter reference spend drops from $100K to $10K/month, so 40% savings ($4K) is less than the $9K fee. | This is the biggest pricing risk. Lead with sovereignty, security and observability rather than savings alone. Re-band the tiers, since cheaper tokens usually raise usage. Push network bundles. |
| **Added: hyperscalers make native routing free** | Price pressure on the base tier, about −10 to −20% on fees. | Compete on cross-cloud, cross-location and network-aware routing plus on-net sovereignty. Move value into the add-ons and the network bundle. |

## Board One-Pager

**Before (connectivity only):** the operator sells enterprise wireline, wireless and SD-WAN connectivity. Enterprise AI traffic rides the network as undifferentiated traffic. The operator captures none of the AI spend and has no software margin on it.

**After (AI-enabled):** DAII adds a software platform fee on top of the existing account. At the assumed mix, an average customer brings about **$500K ARR at about 83% gross margin** (illustrative). That means about **$20M ARR at 40 customers**, plus add-on revenue and stronger network renewal and pull-through.

**Net margin shift:** high-margin, recurring software revenue is layered onto connectivity accounts the operator already serves, so the blended margin of each account rises. The customer's AI spend doesn't flow through DAII, so revenue is not exposed to token-price swings. Customer *value*, however, is exposed to token deflation (see stress tests).
